body: Write short notes on the library services: (i) Selective Dissemination of Information; (ii) Extension library services; (iii) User education; (iv) Inter-library lending and document delivery; (v) Abstracting services.
answer:
> [!answer]
> (i) **SDI**: a customised current-awareness service that **alerts users to new publications** matching their field of study or research interest (profile-based).
> (ii) **Extension services**: taking library services **beyond the library building**, e.g. mobile/book-van libraries, story hours, community outreach.
> (iii) **User education**: **orientation and instruction** (guided tours, information-literacy sessions) for fresh students so they can use the library effectively.
> (iv) **ILL/DD**: borrowing materials from **other libraries** (or obtaining copies of articles) for users when the home library lacks them.
> (v) **Abstracting**: preparing **summaries** of documents so users can decide whether to read the full text.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Define each and add an example.

## Simplified explanation

Alerts, outreach, orientation, borrowing elsewhere, summaries.

body: (a) What is **classification**? (b) Name the two major classification schemes used by libraries. (c) Which is used by most academic libraries in Ghana? (d) State three reasons why library materials are catalogued/organised.
answer:
> [!answer]
> **(a)** Classification is the process of **grouping like entities together and separating unlike ones**: arranging materials so that items on similar subjects sit together, for easy access and retrieval.
>
> **(b)** **Library of Congress Classification (LCC)** and **Dewey Decimal Classification (DDC)**.
>
> **(c)** **Library of Congress** Classification Scheme.
>
> **(d)** To enable (1) a user to find a book whose **author, title or subject** is known; (2) the library to show **what it has** by a given author or on a given subject; (3) a user to find a book by its **edition or character**; (4) to assist **choice** of a book.

body: How can **information literacy skills** contribute to the academic well-being of university undergraduates?
answer:
> [!answer]
> 1. Help students **define their information needs** and focus research.
> 2. Enable **efficient access** to library catalogues, databases and the internet, saving time.
> 3. Build **critical evaluation** skills to avoid fake news and unreliable sources.
> 4. Improve the **quality of assignments and theses** through relevant, current sources.
> 5. Promote **ethical use**: correct citation and referencing, avoiding plagiarism and its sanctions.
> 6. Develop **lifelong, independent learning** and problem-solving skills.
> 7. Increase **employability** and confidence in a knowledge economy.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

## Simplified explanation
